options.text: The process of photosynthesis in leaves
A random movement in response to a stimulus
The production of hormones by plants
A directional growth response towards or away from a stimulus

questions.explanation: A tropism is a directional growth response of a plant towards (positive) or away from (negative) a stimulus such as light or gravity. Tropisms are controlled by plant hormones, particularly auxins.

questions.stem: What is the effect of auxin on shoot cells?

options.text: It inhibits cell elongation
It stimulates cell elongation
It causes cells to die
It causes cell division

questions.explanation: In shoots, auxin stimulates cell elongation, causing cells to grow longer. This is the opposite of its effect in roots, where high concentrations of auxin inhibit cell elongation. This difference is key to understanding tropisms.

questions.stem: In phototropism, auxin moves to the shaded side of a shoot. What happens as a result?

options.text: The shaded side grows less, bending the shoot away from light
The shaded side grows more, bending the shoot towards light
The lit side produces more auxin
Both sides grow equally

questions.explanation: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side of the shoot tip. Since auxin stimulates cell elongation in shoots, the shaded side grows faster than the lit side. This uneven growth causes the shoot to bend towards the light source.

options.text: A growth response towards or away from gravity
A growth response towards or away from light
A growth response towards or away from water
A growth response towards or away from touch

questions.explanation: Gravitropism (also called geotropism) is a directional growth response to gravity. Roots show positive gravitropism (grow towards gravity, downwards) while shoots show negative gravitropism (grow away from gravity, upwards).

questions.stem: Which plant hormone is responsible for fruit ripening?

options.text: Auxin
Cytokinin
Ethene
Gibberellin

questions.explanation: Ethene (ethylene) is a gaseous plant hormone that promotes fruit ripening and leaf fall (abscission). It is produced naturally by ripening fruits, which is why placing an unripe fruit next to a ripe one can speed up ripening.

questions.stem: Where is auxin mainly produced in a plant?

options.text: In the flowers
In the roots
In the shoot tips
In the leaves

questions.explanation: Auxin (specifically indole-3-acetic acid, IAA) is mainly produced in shoot tips, young leaves, and developing seeds. It then moves to other parts of the plant by diffusion and active transport to control growth responses.

questions.stem: What is the role of gibberellins in plants?

options.text: To promote stem elongation and seed germination
To control the opening and closing of stomata
To cause fruit ripening and leaf fall
To inhibit growth and promote dormancy

questions.explanation: Gibberellins promote stem elongation (internode growth) and stimulate seed germination by triggering the production of enzymes that break down starch reserves in the seed. They also play a role in flowering.
